correctness.rationale: The local color-change rule is equivalent to deleting a leaf edge adjacent to an isolate in the white-edge bipartite graph. Every white cycle is permanent; a forest satisfying the exact degree criterion peels to the empty graph, and failure of the criterion prevents any first move. A bipartite Prüfer bijection proves the tree marker weights, the exponential formula proves the forest EGF, the disjoint complement conditions give the six terms, and a Stirling-number count gives minimum-set multiplicities. Independent exhaustive ordinary forcing on 104272 initial subsets in eight rectangular boards matches the criterion, every enumerator coefficient, and the minimum count. Finite checks support but do not replace the all-orders proof.

originality.rationale: The claim is an all-initial-set and all-coefficient classification, stronger than the known minimum-number theorem and distinct from the known maximum-failed-number theorem. Full primary texts with exactly the same underlying graph were inspected for implications, and published-finding corpus alias searches did not reveal a matching complete polynomial. The comparison does not imply universal uniqueness; equivalent formulations under unfamiliar terminology remain a recorded risk.
residual_risks: An earlier exact enumeration under an alternative term, equivalent bipartite incidence representation, or unpublished source cannot be excluded by this finite literature search.
No independent outside mathematical referee has checked the proof; automated finite testing cannot certify arbitrary orders.

value.rationale: A natural dynamical invariant is converted into an exact static incidence-forest condition for every initial set on an infinite two-parameter family. It determines the full zero-forcing polynomial, a nontrivial minimum-set multiplicity and a reusable structural description of successful configurations. Prior scalar extrema alone cannot supply these data; this is a meaningful classification rather than a renaming or an arbitrarily narrow computation.
